thread:
Maya (Support): FYI — Acme reported a sudden spike of 502/504s to the hosted API starting ~10:12 PDT. They see it across multiple models. They supplied a minimal repro and headers. Attaching logs inline.
Maya (Support): Repro curl they ran: `curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME-old\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" -d '{\"input\":\"hi\"}'` -> 502 with empty body.
Maya (Support): Customer claims no change on their side. No deploys on their end. They also saw intermittent 504s when retrying.
Ben (Edge Infra): @Maya can you paste the edge proxy error line(s)? 502s usually mean upstream closed connection or reset.
Maya (Support): Pasted from edge: `[2026-02-14T17:12:34.123Z] envoy error: upstream reset: connection failure, reason: connection termination` and `upstream response code: 502`. Also snippets showing `recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer)` in nginx->upstream.
Carmen (Eng-SRE): Do we have a deploy around 10:12 UTC? I'll check canaries.
Ben (Edge Infra): No infra deploys in that window on edge clusters. I see a sudden spike in short-lived connections to the auth service (auth-svc) from edge at ~17:12Z.
Oliver (Billing): There WAS a scheduled billing token rotation at 17:11:40Z (short key rotation to rotate signing key for API keys). It completed in <1m. We saw a transient queue of validation failures while caches warmed.
Maya (Support): So this could be auth failures being turned into 502s by Envoy because upstream closes? Customer's curl returned 502 not 401.
Carmen (Eng-SRE): That fits: if auth-svc started failing validation and closed connections or returned malformed responses, edge might map that to 502/504 depending on behavior. Can you share edge -> auth svc access logs (full request/response headers)?
Maya (Support): Provided an obfuscated example: `POST /v1/auth/validate  HTTP/1.1" 502 - "-" "x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 0"` and in auth logs: `ERROR: token validation failed: signature mismatch` preceded by `connection reset by peer` entries.
Ben (Edge Infra): Also seeing a lot of `HTTP/2 stream reset` on the h2 pool to auth-svc, consistent with connection churn. h2 connection pool exhausted briefly.
Carmen (Eng-SRE): Steps to reproduce locally: 
```
# simulate rotated key: call validate with old token
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-OLD" https://auth.internal.redwood/v1/validate
# expected: 401/403 or well-formed json error. Observed: connection reset / empty response
```
If auth returns an empty body + connection close, Envoy returns 502.
Ben (Edge Infra): Quick mitigation options: (1) temporarily route auth validation to secondary cluster (auth-legacy) which still accepts old tokens, (2) increase h2 connection limits/keepalive to reduce churn, (3) make auth-svc return 4xx instead of immediately closing connections during rotations.
Oliver (Billing): We can enable a short-lived compatibility mode for 5m that accepts both keys while we roll. Should help. Done at 17:14Z (tracked).
Carmen (Eng-SRE): Please also confirm that auth-svc isn't returning `Connection: close` on 4xx. If it returns a proper 401/403 body, Envoy will pass 401 to client, not 502.
Maya (Support): Customer responded: errors dropped off around 17:16Z after Oliver's change, they were able to retry successfully. They provided post-change curl which returned 200.
Ben (Edge Infra): For longer term: we need to harden edge mapping so upstream auth failures are surfaced as 401/403 where possible. Also plan: add a short retry with jitter for upstream validate calls that error with ECONNRESET (but only for idempotent validation calls).
Carmen (Eng-SRE): Action items: 
- Carmen: open runbook PR to document auth rotations and required graceful-failure behavior (return well-formed 4xx, don't `Connection: close`) — assigned.
- Ben: evaluate h2 pool defaults and safe bump to reduce transient exhaustion during rotations — assigned.
- Oliver: coordinate future rotations with edge infra 15m lead time so we can pre-warm caches / enable compatibility mode — assigned.
- Maya: send customer confirmation + apology and brief RCA update.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout starting: `edgeroute/auth-fallback` -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% (automated) :rocket:
Ben (Edge Infra): Canary showed no extra 502s once auth-compat was on. Will follow up with cluster config diff.
Maya (Support): Customer marked as resolved at 17:20Z. They appreciated the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
Carmen (Eng-SRE): Filing a short postmortem, will include timeline, logs, and the fix (auth compatibility + edge guardrails). Leaving notes to include a small monitoring alert for `upstream reset` spikes to auth cluster.
Maya (Support): Thanks all. Closing thread once postmortem links added.
